GUIDE

Claude Code Guide: Setup, First Task and Review

Start by understanding the code, then make one reviewable change. Keep the task small enough to inspect the result and verify the behavior yourself.

SIMY · Updated 2026-10-04

On this page

  1. What is Claude Code for?

  5. Keep exploring
  6. Sources

What is Claude Code for?

Claude Code is an AI development tool for inspecting code, editing files and running commands. The official documentation describes terminal, IDE, desktop and web surfaces. This guide focuses on getting started from a terminal.

Its purpose differs from a general Claude conversation or organizing office work with Cowork. Keep track of the files and commands involved in the development task.

  • Read the general Claude guide
  • Read the Cowork guide

Follow official setup and confirm the project

Use the official Quickstart for your operating system and follow its authentication steps. Account requirements and limits depend on the connection you use, so check the current official instructions.

After installation, check claude --version and start it from the intended project directory. Protect existing edits and follow the project's branch or worktree policy.

claude --version
cd /path/to/your/project
git status --short
claude
  • Read the official Quickstart

Ask it to explain the code first

Inspect the files in the explanation, then request one bounded change. For a success-message improvement, preserve submission logic and ask for a check of the actual screen. Distinguish a description of the code from evidence that a change was made.

Investigate how contact form submission works in this project. Identify the files for validation, submission and the success message, with references to the code. Do not edit files yet.

Example request

Review commands and the diff before proceeding

Judge permission requests by the files, commands and external effects involved. Inspect the requested behavior, failure states and preserved logic as well as the test result.

Use the Git diff to look for unintended changes and complete the required tests and review. Continue to the SIMY Delivery Loop guide for a coordinated development workflow, or the SQM guide to check a diff against registered safeguards.
